approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted task-local observations. It draws breeding parents from score-ranked quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations, and keeps a bounded greedy survivor population. Before evaluation it builds a fresh surplus pool, verifies canonical identities and rejects newly introduced outside-envelope sulfur signatures relative to their maximum multiplicity in the actual scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the full chronological accepted archive uses folded Morgan integer counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. Its correlated function draws select the announced batch; only real accepted feedback changes survivors and the next fit.
approach.novelty: Replace the allocation residual law by the conditional covariance of the fixed exponential count-Tanimoto model, while keeping the original model's predictive mean. This changes residual variances and dependence together, allowing exploration to move without changing same-state mean ranking. The Parent has no completed direct siblings in the brief. The deliberately complementary parallel test changes the mean while retaining original residuals; the earlier full exponential substitution changed both outputs on an ungated Parent and lost endpoint score. This hybrid has not been evaluated and does not identify a factorial interaction.

hypothesis: Modify only the allocation residual output law on sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180: retain the exact original dot-product count-Tanimoto raw mean mu_DP and replace its standardized latent conditional residual covariance C_DP with C_E from the fixed kernel K_E=exp(T_DP-1). Actual draws are mu_DP[None,:] + score_scale * (Z @ chol(C_E + active_jitter*I).T), using the one original batch-by-pool standard-normal array Z and inherited sequential masks/first-index ties. Active marginal SD is score_scale*sqrt(clamp_min(diag(C_E),0)); original means and truthful exponential SDs reach emission and next-fit probe diagnostics. This is one hybrid Gaussian allocation law replacing residual variance and dependence together, not a correlation-only change or the posterior of a single GP kernel.

finding_summary.headline: Residual exploration changed choices but lost 0.02971 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: The residual substitution was exposed strongly enough to test the route: its loss cannot be explained by an unchanged allocator, an incorrect mean path, missing feedback or a timeout. This narrows the uncertainty: more local wins and genuinely new productive cores can arise from lower-quality sources and still yield smaller total progress and worse endpoints. Later use did not repair that problem. All 2,519 positively supported Child sources were distinguished from 1,681 nonterminal sources without support; 52 supported sources were never drawn, and the 150 terminal records had no later opportunity. These are opportunity and use observations, not independent ancestral credit. The molecular assessment finds diverse ring-rich families rather than global scaffold collapse, but sulfur-halogen incidence fell from 93 to 8 while nitrogen-halogen incidence rose from 786 to 938, oxygen-halogen from 217 to 262 and carbon allenes from 11 to 148. Questionable attachments, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist among high scores. Those associations help explain why novelty and a narrow sulfur admission gate cannot certify chemical quality; they do not prove chemical mediation of the endpoint loss. The exact residual route ends under its registered rule. The passive exponential-mean diagnostic does not license choosing a post-result hybrid. The old full exponential experiment used an ungated Parent, so this test and its complementary sibling do not establish a current-Parent factorial interaction, component additivity or transfer. Current Parent composition remains awaiting catalog review, and broader foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial-lineage-composition and full-history gaps remain open.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-6ebafca203bf produces recognizable azaaryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aromatic regions combined with aliphatic amines, nitrogen/carbonyl medium rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Different seeds reach different families, but leaders within a seed commonly differ only in halogen attachments, short chains or local ring closures. The chemistry is neither acyclic nor globally collapsed. Digest ring-closure-string incidences range from 0.9713 to 0.9885 and aromatic-string incidences from 0.9632 to 0.9828; these measure molecule-level text presence, not aromatic atom fraction or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are zero on every task. Perceived generated median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 35, 29, 29 and 27, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27. All 15 Child and 15 published accepted Parent trajectories were read, each containing 300 observations including ten initial records. There are 4350 generated observations per node. No paths, tasks or paired seeds are absent. context.comparison independently states child_complete=true, paired_complete=true and no profile mismatches; Parent is n-1744a1494180. RDKit parses every generated record, which establishes representability only. Counts over those records find direct N-halogen bonds in Child 938 versus Parent 786, O-halogen bonds in 262 versus 217, and carbon allenes in 148 versus 11. Sulfur-halogen bonds decrease from 93 to 8; that does not make the residual nitrogen/oxygen attachments or ring geometry conventional. Unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres occur in 2015 Child records versus 2455 Parent records, with no explicit @ notation in either. This count excludes axial alkene/allene identity and does not establish stable configurations. Sixty-nine Child records versus 82 Parent records have at most three heavy atoms. Local-bond and geometry flags are observations, not synthesis, toxicity or stability measurements. Scores remain evaluator labels and the complete paired molecular contrasts are descriptive. Passive choices, rejected candidates and their hypothetical continued chemistry have no labels here. The inherited sulfur admission condition constrains a narrow local representation and can permit inherited exceptions; this report does not reconstruct its reference multiplicities or attribute chemistry to that gate or to either predictor output. Its activation belongs to analyze. Current Anchor composition remains needs_review pending prescribed catalog review. Whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial L07 composition and incomplete full-history gaps remain unresolved. Published earlier molecular assessments were read through the legal evidence_index for gap provenance, not pooled as additional matched trials. per_task.generated_character: Compact fused indole/azaindole-like aromatic regions linked through an amide to pyridyl groups dominate. Generated median size is 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with three aromatic rings; most have alkyl/alkenyl and ether substitution. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders each have 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Both carry an N-halogen amide, while seed 1 also puts fluorine directly on the fused ring nitrogen. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom carbon-bridged fused framework with pyridyl amide, methoxy and isopropenyl groups; RDKit perceives five rings including dependent closures, not five independent aromatic systems. Its bridge geometry and unassigned centre require examination. Final seed-2 proposals keep this family but alter carbonyl, nitrogen and halogen attachments. These are medicinally recognizable arrangements with questionable local substitutions and dense closure variants, not a demonstrated synthesis.

The non-N-halogen alternative introduces carbon bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; removing one suspicious bond does not establish credible whole-molecule geometry.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted task-local observations. It draws breeding parents from score-ranked quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations, and keeps a bounded greedy survivor population. Before evaluation it builds a fresh surplus pool, verifies canonical identities and rejects newly introduced outside-envelope sulfur signatures relative to their maximum multiplicity in the actual scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the full chronological accepted archive uses folded Morgan integer counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. Its correlated function draws select the announced batch; only real accepted feedback changes survivors and the next fit.
approach.novelty: Replace the allocation residual law by the conditional covariance of the fixed exponential count-Tanimoto model, while keeping the original model's predictive mean. This changes residual variances and dependence together, allowing exploration to move without changing same-state mean ranking. The Parent has no completed direct siblings in the brief. The deliberately complementary parallel test changes the mean while retaining original residuals; the earlier full exponential substitution changed both outputs on an ungated Parent and lost endpoint score. This hybrid has not been evaluated and does not identify a factorial interaction.

Later-use falsifier: purported useful sources never enter actual positive-support breeding and accepted productive descendants, membership is conflated with use, positive-but-undrawn sources/zero-support records are omitted, or overlapping ancestry is counted as independent effects. Terminal/nonuse falsifier: terminal observations are claimed to have future fitting or breeding evidence, last-batch censoring is treated as avoidable nonuse, absent cohorts/controls are invented, or nonterminal no-support and supported-but-undrawn cases are merged. Outcome falsifier: a complete exposed matched panel with paired mean gain below the frozen +0.002 fails the performance prediction and ends this exact route; retain all task/seed signs and receipt failures.
